newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - EMU worries to weigh on German stocks.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - EMU worries to weigh on German stocks.

text.p: Equity analysts expect sluggish German stock market growth in 1997 with uncertainties over European economic and monetary union (EMU) weighing heavily, a Reuters poll showed on Wednesday.
The six analysts who took part in the poll, which was conducted last week, predicted on average that the DAX-30 would end 1997 at around 3,400 points, a slight drop from the March 12 close of 3,415.

On March 11, the German market reached its all-time closing high of 3,475, but the economic powerhouse of Europe is beset by worries over its quest to meet the criteria for currency union, due to start on January 1, 1999.

Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said on Tuesday he saw little chance that Bonn would be able to cut its budget deficit to three percent of gross domestic product -- a requirement for membership of the currency club. He said failure to do so would mean delaying EMU.
The German stock market would be expected to fall sharply if Germany failed to fulfil the Maastricht criteria, but some analysts said EMU woes were only a temporary burden.

"European monetary union will not turn out to be a long term burden. All this talk depresses stock prices. But the economic situation is steadily improving, and this...should make profit expectations improve."

"We expect a year-end figure of 3,400 if monetary union continues to develop as planned. If monetary union does not go ahead as planned, there is the possibility that the mark will become a strong currency again. But at the moment the mark is weak...today higher profits are possible and that is fundamentally a positive goal for the German economy."
